## University
### Fordham University
After graduating from NYMA, Trump considered attending the [University of Southern California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Southern_California "University of Southern California")'s [film school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USC_School_of_Cinematic_Arts "USC School of Cinematic Arts") to study film,[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher201745-67)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-71) but chose to enroll at [Fordham University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fordham_University "Fordham University"), a private Jesuit [research university](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_university "Research university") in [the Bronx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bronx "The Bronx"), because it was nearer to his parents' home.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlair2000239-72) His decision disappointed his father, Fred, who preferred that Trump attend the [Wharton School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wharton_School "Wharton School") of the [University of Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Pennsylvania "University of Pennsylvania"), an institution that his brother [Freddy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Trump_Jr. "Fred Trump Jr.") had likewise rejected. Trump's sister [Maryanne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryanne_Trump_Barry "Maryanne Trump Barry") privately said that she had helped get him into Fordham.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTECraigBuettner202472-73) Trump commuted from Jamaica Estates to Fordham's campus. As a freshman, Trump's wealth and military background put him at a distance from other students, as did his abstinence from smoking and drinking. He joined the school's squash team that year and sought to integrate himself into the culture.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlair2000239%E2%80%93240-74) At Fordham, he studied economics.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-75) At the school, two friends introduced him to the game of golf, which he grew to love. # About President Tetlow
## Tania Tetlow
![President Tania Tetlow](https://www.fordham.edu/media/home/admin-use-only/leadership/ttetlow_2026_th.jpg)
Tania Tetlow has served as the 33rd president of Fordham University since July 2022, when she became the first layperson and first woman to hold the office since Fordham’s founding in 1841. Tetlow is a legal scholar and former assistant U.S. attorney with a strong commitment to the transformative power of Jesuit education.
President Tetlow has deepened Fordham’s ambitions as the Jesuit University of New York, making major new investments in STEM in connection with the University’s strengths in the humanities and professions. 
In 2024, she oversaw the completion of Fordham’s $350 million Cura Personalis Campaign, which surpassed its goal, raising more than $370 million to enhance the student experience. And in 2025, she was instrumental in securing a $100 million gift—the largest in Fordham’s history—from alumni Maurice (Mo) and Carolyn Dursi Cunniffe. The gift will be used to break ground on a cutting-edge, integrated science facility on the Rose Hill campus and to launch and expand STEM degree programs.
For her leadership in Catholic higher education, President Tetlow received _Commonweal_ magazine’s inaugural Centennial Award in 2024. She serves as board chair of the National Association of Independent Colleges and Universities and is the former chair of the Association of Jesuit Colleges and Universities. Additionally, she teaches strategy in the annual Harvard Seminar for New Presidents.
Prior to Fordham, Tetlow served as the 17th president of Loyola University New Orleans for four years, the first woman and the first layperson to lead that institution. Under her leadership, Loyola completed a turnaround to recover from the most challenging period in its financial history. The university improved its bond rating and repositioned its finances through careful budgeting, increased retention, continued enrollment growth, and expansion of online, graduate, and professional programs. She led this turnaround while navigating multiple hurricanes and the COVID-19 pandemic.

### Early life
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tania_Tetlow&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early life")]
Tetlow was born in New York to L. Mulry Tetlow, a clinical psychologist and psychology professor as well as a former [Jesuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesuits "Jesuits") priest, and Elisabeth Meier Tetlow, a [biblical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bible "Bible") scholar and author.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tania_Tetlow#cite_note-wedding-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tania_Tetlow#cite_note-nola-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tania_Tetlow#cite_note-advocate-5) Her parents met while graduate students at Fordham University.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tania_Tetlow#cite_note-americafirst-6) She was raised in [New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans "New Orleans") and attended [Benjamin Franklin High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Franklin_High_School_\(New_Orleans\) "Benjamin Franklin High School \(New Orleans\)") there and was a recipient of the [National Merit Scholarship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Merit_Scholarship_Program "National Merit Scholarship Program"). Tetlow attended [Tulane University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulane_University "Tulane University") on a Dean's Honor Scholarship beginning at age 16. She was a [Truman Fellow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_S._Truman_Scholarship "Harry S. Truman Scholarship") in 1991 and graduated _cum laude_ in 1992. She graduated _magna cum laude_ from [Harvard Law School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_Law_School "Harvard Law School") in 1995.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tania_Tetlow#cite_note-CV-7)
